Create source-grounded retrieval evaluation questions. Return JSON {"items":[...]}.
For EACH supplied source return {"id":same id,"en":English patient question,"zh":Chinese patient question,
"evidence_id":the exact id string of ONE supplied evidence_options entry supporting BOTH questions}.
Ask one concrete question about a supported detail (cause, symptom, prevention, evaluation, management).
The two questions express the SAME information need, not two facts. Use ordinary patient language.
Include enough topic context to identify the condition but do not copy a source sentence into the question.
Select an evidence option and ask about a concrete detail stated in that option. Do not ask for a personalized dose or individual diagnosis. Do not invent content. No answers in questions.
These are synthetic topic-source retrieval labels, not a clinician-authored benchmark.

[{"id": "MLP-291", "title": "Hypothermia", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Cold weather can affect your body in different ways."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "You can get frostbite , which is an injury to the body that is caused by freezing."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Your body can also lose heat faster than you can produce it."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "That can cause hypothermia, or abnormally low body temperature."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "It can make you sleepy, confused, and clumsy."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Because it happens gradually and affects your thinking, you may not realize you need help."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "A body temperature below 95 °F (35 °C) is a medical emergency and can lead to death if not treated promptly."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Anyone who spends much time outdoors in cold weather can get hypothermia."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "You can also get it from being cold and wet, or under cold water for too long."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Babies and old people are especially at risk."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Babies can get it from sleeping in a cold room."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "Centers for Disease Control and Prevention"}]}, {"id": "MLP-3038", "title": "Ostomy", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "An ostomy is surgery to create an opening (stoma) from an area inside the body to the outside."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "It treats certain diseases of the digestive or urinary systems."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "It can be permanent, when an organ must be removed."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "It can be temporary, when the organ needs time to heal."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "The organ could be the small intestine, colon, rectum, or bladder."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "With an ostomy, there must be a new way for wastes to leave the body."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "There are many different types of ostomy."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Some examples are: Ileostomy - the bottom of the small intestine (ileum) is attached to the stoma."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "This bypasses the colon, rectum and anus."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Colostomy - the colon is attached to the stoma."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Urostomy - the tubes that carry urine to the bladder are attached to the stoma."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "NIH: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases"}]}, {"id": "MLP-365", "title": "Polio and Post-Polio Syndrome", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Polio, or poliomyelitis, is a disease that spreads from person to person."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "In serious cases, it can cause paralysis (where you can't move parts of the body)."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "The paralysis may be lifelong and can sometimes be life-threatening."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Because of vaccines, polio is rare in the United States."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "But polio does occur in some parts of the world, and travelers can spread the virus."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "It spreads through contact with: The stool (poop) of person who has the infection Droplets from a sneeze or cough of someone who has the infection This contact can happen if: You get contaminated stool or droplets on your hands and then touch your mouth A child puts contaminated toys or other objects into their mouth You share food or utensils with someone who has the infection People who have the infection can spread it to others just before and up to several weeks after the symptoms appear."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "People who don't have symptoms can still spread the virus to others and make them sick."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Polio mainly affects children under age 5."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "But people of any age (including adults) who are unvaccinated are at risk of developing polio."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "People who live in or travel to areas where there is polio are more likely to get polio."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Most people who get infected with poliovirus do not have any symptoms."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "But one out of four people who get polio will have flu-like symptoms."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "These symptoms usually last 2 to 5 days, and they include: Sore throat Fever Fatigue Nausea Headache Stomach pain In rare cases, polio can be very serious."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "It can lead to: Meningitis , an infection of the covering of your spinal cord and/or brain."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Weakness or paralysis in your arms, legs, or both."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "This paralysis or weakness can last a lifetime."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "It is possible for the paralysis to become life-threatening if it affects the muscles that you use to breathe."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "Post-polio syndrome (PPS), which happens later in life."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "Post-polio syndrome (PPS) is a condition that affects polio survivors many years after they recovered from polio."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "People who get PPS start having new weakening in muscles that were previously affected by the polio infection."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "Symptoms may range from mild to serious."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "The symptoms of PPS include: Muscle weakness Muscle atrophy (wasting away of muscles) Loss of muscle function Mental and physical fatigue Joint pain Curving of the spine ( scoliosis ) PPS is rarely life-threatening, but the symptoms can interfere with your daily life."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "If you think you or someone in your family has symptoms of polio, call your healthcare provider right away or go to an emergency room."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "To find out if you or your child has polio, the provider: Will do a physical exam."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "Will take a detailed medical history, including your vaccination history and history of any recent travel."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "Will collect samples of body fluids, such as stool, saliva, blood, urine, and spinal fluid."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "Poliovirus is most likely to be detected in stool specimens."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "May do an MRI to look at pictures of the spinal cord."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "What are the treatments for polio and post-polio syndrome (PPS)?"}, {"id": "S029", "text": "There is no cure or specific treatment for polio."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "For a mild case, getting rest and drinking plenty of liquids may help with some of the symptoms."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "If the polio is more serious, you or your child may need: Physical or occupational therapy to help with arm or leg weakness."}, {"id": "S032", "text": "The earlier therapy is started, the better."}, {"id": "S033", "text": "Pain relievers to help with pain and treat fever."}, {"id": "S034", "text": "If your child is sick, do not give them aspirin unless their provider tells you to."}, {"id": "S035", "text": "A ventilator to help with breathing if the breathing muscles are weak or paralyzed."}, {"id": "S036", "text": "Treatments may help you manage your symptoms."}, {"id": "S037", "text": "They include: Non-fatiguing exercises (exercises that do not cause pain or fatigue that lasts more than 10 minutes)."}, {"id": "S038", "text": "These exercises may improve muscle strength and reduce tiredness."}, {"id": "S039", "text": "Your provider can help you figure out which exercises are best for you."}, {"id": "S040", "text": "Lifestyle changes, such as eating a healthy diet, getting enough sleep, and not smoking."}, {"id": "S041", "text": "There are two types of vaccine that can prevent polio: Inactivated poliovirus vaccine (IPV) given as an injection in the leg or arm, depending on how old you are."}, {"id": "S042", "text": "Since 2000, this has been the only polio vaccine used in the United States."}, {"id": "S043", "text": "Oral poliovirus vaccine (OPV) is given as drops in the mouth."}, {"id": "S044", "text": "It is still used throughout much of the world."}, {"id": "S045", "text": "Children in the United States get four doses of PV as part of their routine childhood immunizations ."}, {"id": "S046", "text": "Most adults in the United States were vaccinated against polio as children."}, {"id": "S047", "text": "It may be given to adults who have completed their polio vaccinations but are at higher risk of contact with poliovirus."}, {"id": "S048", "text": "You may be at higher risk if you are: Traveling to a country where the risk of getting polio is greater Working in a laboratory or healthcare setting and handling samples that might contain polioviruses A healthcare worker who has contact with patients who could have polio Another way to help prevent the spread of polio is to wash your hands often with soap and water."}, {"id": "S049", "text": "Alcohol-based hand sanitizers will not kill poliovirus."}, {"id": "S050", "text": "Centers for Disease Control and Prevention"}]}, {"id": "MLP-5", "title": "Heart Attack", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Each year almost 800,000 Americans have a heart attack."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "A heart attack happens when blood flow to the heart suddenly becomes blocked."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Without the blood coming in, the heart can't get oxygen."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "If not treated quickly, the heart muscle begins to die."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "But if you do get quick treatment, you may be able to prevent or limit damage to the heart muscle."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "That's why it's important to know the symptoms of a heart attack and call 911 if you or someone else is having them."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "You should call, even if you are not sure that it is a heart attack."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "The most common symptoms in men and women are: Chest discomfort."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "It is often in center or left side of the chest."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "It usually lasts more than a few minutes."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "It can feel like pressure, squeezing, fullness, or pain ."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "It also can feel like heartburn or indigestion."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "You may get it before or during the chest discomfort."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "It can happen when you are resting or doing a little bit of physical activity."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "You may feel pain or discomfort in one or both arms, the back, shoulders, neck, jaw, or upper part of the stomach."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "You may also have other symptoms, such as nausea, vomiting, dizziness, and lightheadedness."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "Sometimes women will have different symptoms then men."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "For example, they are more likely to feel tired for no reason."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "The most common cause of heart attacks is coronary artery disease (CAD)."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "With CAD, there is a buildup of cholesterol and other material, called plaque, on their inner walls or the arteries."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "Eventually an area of plaque can rupture (break open)."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "A blood clot can form around the plaque and block the artery."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "A less common cause of heart attack is a severe spasm (tightening) of a coronary artery."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "The spasm cuts off blood flow through the artery."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "At the hospital, health care providers make a diagnosis based on your symptoms, blood tests, and different heart health tests ."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "Treatments may include medicines and medical procedures such as coronary angioplasty ."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "After a heart attack, cardiac rehabilitation and lifestyle changes can help you recover."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "NIH: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute"}]}, {"id": "MLP-1233", "title": "Addison Disease", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Your adrenal glands are just above your kidneys."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "The outside layer of these glands makes hormones that help your body respond to stress and regulate your blood pressure and water and salt balance."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Addison disease happens if the adrenal glands don't make enough of these hormones."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "A problem with your immune system usually causes Addison disease."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "The immune system mistakenly attacks your own tissues, damaging your adrenal glands."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Other causes include infections and cancer."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Symptoms include: Weight loss Muscle weakness Fatigue that gets worse over time Low blood pressure Patchy or dark skin Lab tests can confirm that you have Addison disease."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "You will need to take hormone pills for the rest of your life."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "If you have Addison disease, you should carry an emergency ID."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "It should say that you have the disease, list your medicines and say how much you need in an emergency."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "NIH: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases"}]}]
